Dubai Police bust 'luxury car beggar', arrest 37 beggars of various nationalities amid crackdown
item.description: Dubai Police are cracking down on beggars during Ramadan. Authorities have arrested dozens of people exploiting the holy month's charitable spirit. This crackdown is part of an annual campaign to prevent illegal solicitation. Similar efforts are underway across the UAE. Residents are urged to donate through official charities to ensure aid reaches those truly in need.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Flights resume at Abu Dhabi's Zayed International Airport: What travellers must know now amid Iran-US-Israel war
item.description: Abu Dhabi's Zayed International Airport has resumed limited flight operations, offering relief to thousands of stranded passengers after days of severe travel disruptions amid Iran-US-Israel war. This cautious reopening follows widespread flight suspensions triggered by escalating geopolitical tensions, with authorities prioritizing passenger safety and operational readiness during the gradual recovery.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE opens ‘safe air corridors’: Airlines allowed 48 flights per hour amid Middle East tensions
item.description: The UAE has opened 'safe air corridors' allowing up to 48 flights hourly to stabilise regional aviation amidst geopolitical tensions and the Iran-US-Israel war. This initiative aims to restore connectivity, evacuate thousands of stranded passengers and support tourism and business sectors. Limited commercial services have resumed, with authorities planning further phases to clear the backlog.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai's KHDA moves Indian schools to distance learning till term end amid US-Israel war on Iran
item.description: Dubai's education regulator has extended distance learning for Indian curriculum schools until the end of the academic term. This decision, impacting CBSE and ICSE students, is a precautionary measure amid regional security concerns due to the Iran-Israel-US war. The new academic year will commence on April 6, 2026, ensuring continuity and safety for thousands of students.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Over 60% turnout as Nepal votes in 'historic' polls powered by Gen Z
item.description: Nepal's Gen Z voters turned out in large numbers for snap parliamentary elections, a significant development following September protests that reshaped the country's politics. Despite logistical challenges in the mountainous nation, preliminary turnout exceeded 60%, with young activists viewing election day as the next phase of their movement for change and accountability.
item.dc:creator: Vishant Agarwala

item.title: Abu Dhabi on edge: 6 injured as drone debris from Iran and US-Israel conflict crashes into industrial zone
item.description: Six people were injured in Abu Dhabi by falling drone debris after air defences intercepted projectiles amid escalating Iran-Israel-US tensions. This incident highlights the risks of falling fragments even during successful interceptions. The UAE is urging residents to stay informed and follow safety advisories as regional conflicts spill into civilian areas.

item.title: UAE emergency alert: 5 things to do, one to never do if you see falling shrapnel or missile debris amid US-Israel war on Iran
item.description: Missile interceptions are now a reality for Gulf residents. Fragments from intercepted threats are falling, causing injuries and damage. Authorities in the UAE are issuing crucial safety advice. Residents must stay calm, move away from debris, seek shelter indoors and report any findings immediately. Never touch or approach suspicious objects. Official updates are vital for safety during these uncertain times.

item.title: Young GOP activists used racial slurs, discussed killing Black Americans in WhatsApp chat: Report
item.description: A WhatsApp group of young Republicans, led by a local party secretary, reportedly featured hundreds of racial slurs and discussions of murdering Black Americans. Members also hurled antisemitic and misogynistic insults. The group's activities are now under criminal investigation, with party leadership calling for immediate resignations.

item.title: UAE shocked as fruit and vegetable prices rise amid US-Israel war on Iran: What shoppers need to know
item.description: UAE shoppers are facing rising fruit and vegetable prices, attributed to geopolitical tensions amid Iran-US-Israel war, impacting shipping and air freight. Despite stable supply chains, increased fuel, transport and insurance costs are pushing up prices for perishable goods. While authorities assure food security remains strong, consumers may see continued price fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Have to be involved in appointment of next Iranian leader': Trump calls Khamenei's son Mojtaba 'unacceptable', 'lightweight'
item.description: President Trump declared he will personally select Iran's next leader, deeming Ali Khamenei's son, Mojtaba, "unacceptable." Trump stated he must be involved in the appointment, comparing it to Venezuela, to ensure a leader who brings peace, not war. This comes amid a US military campaign targeting Iran's capabilities, not regime change.

item.title: US asked Ukraine for help against Iranian drones in Middle East, says Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukraine has agreed to share its expertise and interceptor drone technology to help the US counter Iranian attacks in the Middle East. President Zelenskyy emphasized that this assistance will only be provided if it doesn't compromise Ukraine's own defense and strengthens diplomatic ties. He also suggested a potential drone-for-missile swap with Gulf allies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump ‘furious’ after Kristi Noem claims he approved $220 million DHS ad campaign: Report
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem's testimony about a $220 million ad campaign, featuring her face and reportedly approved by President Trump, has sparked White House fury. Senator John Kennedy questioned the approval process, leading to reports of Trump considering Noem's replacement, with Markwayne Mullin's name surfacing. Noem also faced scrutiny over contracts and her association with Corey Lewandowski.
